item.title: Awa Odori: Japan's Greatest Dance Festival — Guide
item.description: Awa Odori is the most famous dance festival in Japan and the pride of Tokushima, held each year during the mid-August Obon season and drawing well over a million spectators. Over four days and nights, the streets of Tokushima city fill with ‘ren’ — dance troupes of choreographed performers, some over a hundred strong — parading and dancing to the driving, hypnotic rhythm of taiko drums, shamisen, flutes and bells. The dance has a distinctive loose, flowing style, with dancers in colourful yukata and the women in half-moon straw hats, all chanting the famous refrain: ‘the dancing fool and the watching fool are both fools, so you might as well dance!

item.title: Yosakoi Festival, Kochi: Japan's Great Dance Fest — Guide
item.description: Yosakoi is Kochi’s gift to Japan: a dynamic, modern dance festival born here in 1954 that has since spread across the whole country and beyond. Held every August, the Kochi Yosakoi Festival transforms the city into a stage as around two hundred teams — tens of thousands of dancers in dazzling matching costumes — parade and dance through the streets to pounding music that blends traditional and modern sounds. Each dancer wields naruko, small wooden clappers that click in rhythm, and every team choreographs its own energetic routine, competing for prizes across multiple venues.
